guideposts.label: Unprecedented La Vuelta stage towns in a familiar area
guideposts.detail: Alcaraz and Elche de la Sierra stage towns making their first appearance in La Vuelta this year. The full list: Monaco (stage 1), Manosque (2), Font-Romeu (stage 3), Falset (5), Roquetes (5), Vall d’Alba (7), Puçol (8), Xeraco (8), La Vila Joiosa (9), Alcaraz (10), Elche de la Sierra (10), Vera (12), Almuñécar (13), Palma del Rio (15), Cortegana (16), La Rábida (16), Dos Hermanas (17), El Puerto d

guideposts.label: 2 non-starters
guideposts.detail: There are 168 riders in the peloton as George Bennett (NSN) and Henri-François Renard-Haquin (Picnic PostNL) don't start.

guideposts.label: Polka dot jersey
guideposts.detail: Santiago Buitrago is the first Colombian leader of the mountains standings of La Vuelta since Nairo Quintana after stages 11 and 12 in 2016. At the time, Quintana was wearing La Roja. The last Colombian rider to wear the polka dot jersey during a La Vuelta stage is Walter Pedraza on day 3 in 2015. His compatriot Esteban Chaves was leading the mountains standings but he raced with La Roja. Buitrago

guideposts.label: Team standings
guideposts.detail: With Felix Gall (4th), Gregor Muhlberger (12th) and Matthew Riccitello (16th) battling at the front up the Alto de Aitana, Decathlon CMA CGM extended their lead in the team standings to 42’30’’ on Netcompany Ineos and 49’34’’ on Visma-Lease a Bike.

guideposts.label: First attacks
guideposts.detail: A lone attacker leads the way at km 2.

guideposts.label: More movement
guideposts.detail: The loneleader was caught at km 3. It's a four-rider group leading the way.

guideposts.label: The attackers are caught at km 6
guideposts.detail: Today could favour fast men or long range attackers depending on the scenario. Many riders said the dynamics at the start will be key to establish the race scenario.

guideposts.label: Attacks keep flying...
guideposts.detail: But the bunch is packed at km 8.

guideposts.label: Back together again
guideposts.detail: How long will it take for the breakaway to establish? The answer to that question will also determine their chances of making it to the end.

guideposts.label: 6 new leaders
guideposts.detail: Enzo Paleni (Groupama-FDJ United), Michael Gogl (Alpecin-Premier Tech), Jasha Sütterlin (Jayco AlUla), Fabian Weiss (Tudor), Sinuhé Fernandez (Burgos Burpellet BH) and Ivan Cobo (Kern Pharma) have opened a gap at km 15.

guideposts.label: Dversnes in pursuit
guideposts.detail: Fredrik Dversnes (Uno-X Mobility) tries to make it a seven-man breakaway.

guideposts.label: The situation at km 20
guideposts.detail: Enzo Paleni (Groupama-FDJ United), Michael Gogl (Alpecin-Premier Tech), Jasha Sütterlin (Jayco AlUla), Fabian Weiss (Tudor), Sinuhé Fernandez (Burgos Burpellet BH) and Ivan Cobo (Kern Pharma) lead the way. +37'' Fredrik Dversnes (Uno-X Mobility) +1'38'' Peloton

guideposts.label: Dversnes joins the 6 leaders
guideposts.detail: After 22 km, Fredrik Dversnes (Uno-X Mobility) has bridged the gap to Enzo Paleni (Groupama-FDJ United), Michael Gogl (Alpecin-Premier Tech), Jasha Sütterlin (Jayco AlUla), Fabian Weiss (Tudor), Sinuhé Fernandez (Burgos Burpellet BH) and Ivan Cobo (Kern Pharma).

guideposts.label: Gap under control?
guideposts.detail: The peloton reach km 24 with a gap of 1'42''. The attackers' lead had previously gone up to 2 minutes.

guideposts.label: The gap increases again
guideposts.detail: At km 35, the peloton trail by 2'05''. Cofidis and Visma-Lease a Bike have been reported to be setting the pace.

guideposts.label: 43.1 km in the first hour
guideposts.detail: The peloton are moving closer on the climb: 2'25'', compared to 2'55'' at the bottom.

guideposts.label: Ben Turner retires
guideposts.detail: The Brit is the second Netcompany Ineos to leave La Vuelta 26 after his compatriot Josh Tarling.

guideposts.label: A stabilised situation
guideposts.detail: After 66 kilmetres, Enzo Paleni (Groupama-FDJ United), Michael Gogl (Alpecin-Premier Tech), Fredrik Dversnes (Uno-X Mobility), Jasha Sütterlin (Jayco AlUla), Fabian Weiss (Tudor), Sinuhé Fernandez (Burgos Burpellet BH) and Ivan Cobo (Kern Pharma) are riding 2'40'' ahead of the bunch.

guideposts.label: How to upset the field?
guideposts.detail: Earlier at La Vuelta 26, Fredrik Dversnes (Uno-X Mobility) gave some indisght based on his personal success in the Giro 2026. He's at the front to try and enforce them today: "It’s about having some bad days to lower other's expectations, then come in a breakaway with rather smaller guys that had much bigger engines than you think, and then you just hammer away and win."

guideposts.label: The gap decreases again on the climb
guideposts.detail: The peloton move closer: 2'05''.

guideposts.label: 100 kilometres to go
guideposts.detail: The average speed after 2 hours: 42.1 km/h. The last gap: 1'48''. Sergio Samitier (Cofidis) is driving the bunch with Steven Kruijswijk (Visma-Lease a Bike) on his wheel.

guideposts.label: Visma | Lease a Bike and Cofidis leading the peloton
The gap increases again after the ascent
guideposts.detail: At km 102, the peloton trail by 1'40''.

guideposts.label: Back to (almost) 2 minutes
guideposts.detail: The seven leaders enter the final 75 kilomeres with a gap of 1'55''.

guideposts.label: Headed to Hellin
guideposts.detail: Hellin (km 125) has been a La Vuelta stage town on a handful of occasions, most recently in 2017. The race headed to Xorret de Cati, where Julian Alaphilippe took his first Grand Tour stage win.

guideposts.label: The average speed after 3 hours: 44.7 km/h
guideposts.detail: The pace seriously increased on more favourable terrain.

guideposts.label: Gogl suffers a mechanical
guideposts.detail: Austria's national champion rapidly returns to the breakaway group, 1'25'' ahead of the peloton.

guideposts.label: Into the final 40 kilometres
guideposts.detail: Magnus Cort (Uno-X Mobility) just returned to the bunch after a mechanical. The Danish all-rounder spoke at the start as he takespart in his last Grand Tour: "I feel ok, I have decent legs and the team is doing really well so I'm enjoying it a lot. We came here with the ambition to chase stages and we already won one, and there are opportunities left; we’re fighting and happy with what we got so f

guideposts.label: Heading for the final climb of the day
guideposts.detail: The seven leaders are five kilometres form the bottom of the ascent up Puerto de Socovos. The last gap: 1'22''.

guideposts.label: Down to 4 leaders
guideposts.detail: Enzo Paleni (Groupama-FDJ United), Michael Gogl (Pinarello Q36.5), Fredrik Dversnes (Uno-X Mobility) and Ivan Cobo (Kern Pharma) are about to begin the final ascent. Jasha Sütterlin (Jayco AlUla), Fabian Weiss (Tudor) and Sinuhé Fernandez (Burgos Burpellet BH) have been dropped on an uncategorised uphill section.

guideposts.label: Some moves in the bunch
guideposts.detail: Some attackers try to make the most of the rolling terrain ahead of the final climb. Matthew Brennan (Visma-Lease a Bike) reacts himself to cover their moves.

guideposts.label: Sivakov insists; Pedersen is distanced
guideposts.detail: Already named the most combative rider on Sunday, Pavel Sivakov (UAE Emirates XRG) is very active. Valentin Paret-Peintre (Soudal Quick-Step) also attacks. Cofidis try to control the situation. Mads Pedersen (Lidl-Trek) is among the riders off the back.

guideposts.label: Dunbar and Barta in pursuit
guideposts.detail: Eddie Dunbar (Pinarello Q36.5) has dropped Valentin Paret-Peintre (Soudal Quick-Step) and is about to be joined by Will Barta (Tudor). They are 45'' behind the five leaders, who face the final 5 kilometres of ascent. The reduced peloton trail by 1 minute.

guideposts.label: Gogl ups the ante into the final 25 kilometres
guideposts.detail: Weiss is dropped. Dunbar still trails by 40''. Barta is caught by the bunch (+55'').

guideposts.label: Vermaerke attacks; Mas reacts
guideposts.detail: As Richard Carapaz (EF Education-EasyPost) and Mattias Skjelmose (Lidl-Trek) followed a move initiated by Kevin Vermaerke (UAE Emirates XRG), Enric Mas (Movistar) moved to close the gap. There are around 20 riders in the bunch. They are half a minute behind the attackers with 23 km to go.

guideposts.label: The chasers are caught
guideposts.detail: The four leaders face the final 17 kilometres with a gap of 20 seconds.

guideposts.label: 2 leaders with 12 km to go
guideposts.detail: Gogl and Dversnes hold on to a 15'' gap.

guideposts.label: Calzoni is caught with 2 km to go
guideposts.detail: Matthew Brennan sets the pace with Enric Mas on his wheel.

guideposts.label: Top 5
guideposts.detail: 1. Bastien Tronchon (Groupama-FDJ United) 2. Magnus Cort (Uno-X Mobility) 3. Thibau Nys (Lidl-Trek) 4. Wout van Aert (Visma-Lease a Bike) 5. Alessandro Romele (XDS Astana)
